hypothesis: The two connect-probe grids on the cold-open path, cut 25ms->5ms by the boot-floor lane (PR #2891, record 20260926-202000), still quantize: the TUI->daemon startup poll (DAEMON_PROBE_INTERVAL_MS=5) fires on EVERY cold daemon launch with a measured EFFECTIVE grid of ~6.2ms (5ms sleep + ~1.2ms probe/scheduler overhead) and bind->connect overshoot uniform over that grid (mean ~2.3ms); the supervisor->worker poll (WORKER_CONNECT_BACKOFF_MS=5 unix) is CONDITIONALLY live: the probe loop starts only after persist_worker (a fresh+sync_all+rename on the worker descriptor), so the grid fires only when that fsync finishes before the worker binds (fast-fsync windows / loaded machines) and is inert when the persist dominates. Cutting both to 1ms (flat fast poll) tightens the effective grid to ~2.2ms and the mean overshoot to ~1.1ms, saving ~1-4ms of pure wait per cold launch on grid 1 and the same where grid 2 fires; no busy-wait cost (the probes are ~us connect attempts between 1ms sleeps).
